extra.label: Binder RMSD (binder alone vs complex)
extra.note: BindCraft Binder_RMSD: the binder predicted on its own, compared with its shape in the complex. BindCraft rejects designs above 3.5 Å.
rescue: Re-predict the binder alone with a second model; discard if it still differs from the complex shape

extra.label: Atoms within 3 Å of the other subunit
extra.note: The design is placed on the reference assembly. A binder that overlaps another subunit could not bind the assembled protein. Overlap fails a design; contact at the subunit interface is a warning.
rescue: Add the other subunit as fixed context, or move the binder to a face that stays exposed in the assembly

nl.text: At most 9 atoms within 3 Å of the other subunit

extra.label: Contacted residues at the subunit interface
extra.note: Contacted residues that another subunit buries in the assembly. A surface that is part of the subunit interface may not exist on the assembled protein.
rescue: Keep as a hedge, or discard if the goal is a binder of the intact assembly

extra.label: Atoms within 3 Å of the rest of the protein
extra.note: BindCraft only saw the construct. The rest of the same chain (the removed regions) is placed from the reference structure; a binder that overlaps it could not bind the full-length protein.
rescue: Include the neighbouring domain in the target, or move the binder away from that face

nl.text: At most 9 atoms within 3 Å of the rest of the protein

extra.label: Contacts next to a cut end
extra.note: Contacted residues within a few residues of a cut end of the construct, or of a deleted loop. A surface next to a cut can be exposed only because the rest of the protein is missing.
rescue: Extend the target by 10 to 15 residues and re-run, or discard

extra.label: Contacted residues buried in the full protein
extra.note: Contacted residues that the removed regions would bury (more than the area set in the profile). These contacts may not exist on the full-length protein.
rescue: Include the covering region in the target and re-run

BindCraft keeps at most 2 accepted sequences per backbone by default. Each run keeps its own settings, hotspots, target construct and diversity estimate.

cards.title: Target frame
cards.html: BindCraft restarts the residue numbering at 1, so the tool maps the numbering of the construct back to the reference structure by sequence. It adds the other subunits and the rest of the chain of the reference structure, and checks every design against them.

cards.title: Read, recomputed, missing
cards.html:
Read: sequences, per-model and average scores, per-residue pLDDT (B-factor), the run settings and the filter counters.
Recomputed from the structures: interface on both chains, H-bonds, buried unsatisfied polars, buried area, hydrophobic patches, loops, termini, liabilities, fold clusters (TM-align), site clusters, overlap with the other subunits and the rest of the chain.
Not available: PAE, ipSAE, an independent pose check, repeat seeds, and often the number of attempted trajectories. The checks that need them are switched off instead of guessed.

text.badge.title.board: Designs and scores come from BindCraft runs. Structures are relaxed AlphaFold2 models, placed on the reference structure. Every score is a screen, not a verdict.
text.badge.title.inspector: Binder models are BindCraft AF2 complexes placed on the reference chain. Contacts, hydrogen bonds, buried polars and context checks are recomputed from the coordinates. BindCraft does not write PAE, so none is shown.
text.badge.title.map: Designs and scores come from BindCraft runs. Where orthologs or paralogs were given, they are UniProt sequences aligned to the target construct and conservation grades are computed from the orthologs only.
text.badge.title.query: Designs and scores come from BindCraft runs, accepted and rejected. Rules are typed and editable; the natural-language box is keyword-based and only fills the same rules.

unevaluated.reason: Binderscope does not map this column to a metric: interchain only, CA atoms only (Backbone_Clashes) or all atoms within 2.5 A (All_Atom_Clashes); one stem cannot hold two counts and neither is BindCraft 1's count

unevaluated.name: Interface_BuriedArea
unevaluated.reason: Binderscope does not map this column to a metric: binder-side buried area only; BindCraft 1's dSASA is the buried area of both partners

unevaluated.reason: Binderscope does not map this column to a metric: binder-side buried area over the free binder's surface; BindCraft 1 divides the buried area of both sides by the binder's area in the complex

filter_set.note: These are the thresholds this campaign recorded in its own metadata, not BindCraft 1's reconstructed defaults. They are screens, not verdicts: a design BindCraft rejected stays rejected, and where its CSV values pass a threshold that BindCraft judged on each validation model the rejection still stands. 4 recorded thresholds on metrics Binderscope does not carry (Backbone_Clashes, Interface_BuriedArea, Interface_BuriedArea_Fraction, Receptor_Chains_Contacted) cannot be re-checked here; BindCraft's own verdict covers them.

62 trajectory folders hold no structures (archive_trajectories is false in the settings); trajectory structures are not read.
13 filters with a finite threshold were read from the metadata (8 mandatory); 17 with an infinite threshold (no limit) were dropped.
.campaign_state.json lists the same 62 trajectory hashes as the table.
No hotspots recorded for this run: its designs have no hotspots touched and no intended epitope, so the epitope checks and the epitope numbers (epi_prec, epi_rec) are left empty.

1 of 222 designs were placed by the whole-target fit: fewer than 12 target residues lie near the binder, so there is nothing to weight the fit around (prov.fit and prov.fit_note of each design say which)

Filters: this run is judged by the 9 thresholds the campaign recorded itself, not by BindCraft 1's reconstructed defaults; 4 recorded thresholds on metrics Binderscope does not carry cannot be re-checked here (Backbone_Clashes, Interface_BuriedArea, Interface_BuriedArea_Fraction, Receptor_Chains_Contacted). A design BindCraft rejected stays rejected even where its CSV values pass a threshold, because BindCraft judges confidence filters on each validation model and the CSV holds the mean.

fold.note: TM-align (tmtools) on the binder CA trace, TM-score x 100 normalised by the shorter chain, over the accepted designs of all runs. Backbones of different runs are compared too; clusters and estimates are formed per run.

epitope.rule: the epitope of a family is every target residue contacted by any of its accepted designs
epitope.note: 21 families: too few to call a trend (estimates are low-confidence below 30 families).

flags.text: 21 families: estimates are shown with low confidence below 30.

BindCraft keeps at most 3 accepted sequences per backbone. 18 of 21 families are at that limit, so their sibling counts are censored (counts of sequences per family are lower bounds); counting families is not affected.

data.cap_source: inferred: highest number of accepted sequences on one backbone

flags.text: Sequences that fail the AlphaFold2 pre-filters leave no row (only a counter, and a sequence counts once per filter it fails), so the sequence-level funnel cannot be reconstructed from the rows.
At TM 0.8 (distance 0.2) 21 of 21 families are separate fold clusters, so the fold count cannot saturate at that setting. Use TM 0.5 for 'same fold'; 0.8 is the 'same backbone' cut.
A restarted BindCraft run resets its own counters (failure_csv.csv) and cannot be detected from the output files; the row order of trajectory_stats.csv is the only generation order available.
Forecasts of new clusters are valid for at most as many further families as already seen (m <= n).
A passing design is a predicted binder, not a measured one.

highlights.text: None of the 58 accepted designs fails the rest-of-protein check (fewer than 10 binder atoms within 3 Å of residues outside the construct, in the reference structure); 3 have at least one atom closer than 2.2 Å.

link.filter: largest overlap: 3 atoms within 3 Å of the rest of the protein

highlights.text: No hotspots recorded for pdl1_minibinder_demo: its designs have no hotspots touched and no intended epitope; the binding-site view (site A1) is built from the residues the designs contact most.

Families, not sequences: pdl1_minibinder_demo has 21 (coverage 1.00, level enough), measured on fold and site together. The estimates for pdl1_minibinder_demo are low-confidence (fewer than 30 families).

Where a tag can go (21 families of pdl1_minibinder_demo, predicted from one conformation). His6: 7 at the C-terminus, 11 at the N-terminus, 3 at either end, 0 at neither. Twin-Strep: 7 at the C-terminus, 11 at the N-terminus, 3 at either end, 0 at neither. BindCraft was not asked to keep the ends free, so the spread is unconstrained.

39 of the 164 rejected designs that have a structure (all in pdl1_minibinder_demo) are near-miss rescues: a single filter missed by at most 25% of its threshold (33 on i_pTM, 5 on binder RMSD and 1 on unbound binder pLDDT). Thresholds on Backbone_Clashes are the campaign's own and were not re-checked here, so a design may also miss one of them.
